mail.diag.unavailable.why: Missing permission or data prevents a reliable conclusion
mail.diag.unavailable.fix: Open diagnostics with an administrator session and inspect the unavailable source
mail.diag.bounded.why: Checks limit each run to ten domains and ten selectors per domain
mail.diag.bounded.fix: Inspect the remaining domains and selectors in MailPlus Server
mail.diag.mailplus.why: MailPlus must be installed and running with SMTP enabled to handle mail
mail.diag.mailplus.fix: Install or start MailPlus Server in Package Center and enable SMTP in its settings
mail.diag.queue.why: Queued messages are awaiting delivery and an unknown age cannot prove a backlog
mail.diag.queue.fix: Inspect queue times and reasons in MailPlus Server without flushing or deleting messages
mail.diag.deferred_dns.why: Delivery needs a resolvable destination or relay hostname
mail.diag.deferred_dns.fix: Check the relay hostname and NAS DNS resolver before retrying delivery
mail.diag.deferred_auth.fix: Use mail setup to review relay authentication without exposing credentials
mail.diag.deferred_tls.fix: Check the relay TLS mode and certificate without disabling verification
mail.diag.deferred_policy.why: Recipient policy or sender reputation prevented delivery
mail.diag.deferred_policy.fix: Inspect the rejection in MailPlus and review SPF, DKIM, DMARC and DNSBL evidence
mail.diag.deferred_remote.why: A temporary recipient failure can recover through normal queue retries
mail.diag.deferred_remote.fix: Keep the queued message and inspect the remote response if retries remain unsuccessful
mail.diag.relay.why: An enabled relay needs to run and a growing queue makes old success evidence relevant
mail.diag.relay.fix: Review the MailPlus Setup Assistant relay service and MailPlus Delivery settings in mail setup
mail.diag.mx.why: Direct receiving needs a valid mail route but missing MX can fall back to address records
mail.diag.mx.fix: Review MX and explicit null MX against the intended direct or routing setup
mail.diag.spf.why: Static SPF checks cannot establish actual sender authorization
mail.diag.spf.fix: Publish one SPF record for the actual sender and review includes and lookup limits
mail.diag.dkim.why: Only configured selectors are checked and DNS keys alone do not prove signing or alignment
mail.diag.dkim.fix: Match the actual signing selector to its DNS public key and verify a delivered message separately
mail.diag.dmarc.why: Exact-domain DMARC checks do not evaluate inherited organizational policy
mail.diag.dmarc.fix: Review the exact and parent DMARC policies after confirming SPF or DKIM alignment
mail.diag.mtasts.why: MTA-STS is optional and this check reads only its TXT record
mail.diag.mtasts.fix: If MTA-STS is intended, validate its TXT and HTTPS policy, certificate and MX coverage
mail.diag.tlsrpt.why: TLS-RPT is optional and TXT presence does not prove report delivery
mail.diag.tlsrpt.fix: If reports are intended, validate the TLS-RPT rua destination and external authorization
mail.diag.egress.why: Two agreeing sources are required and HTTP egress may differ from SMTP routing
mail.diag.egress.fix: Review NAS connectivity and routing without assuming that an unobserved IP family is disabled
mail.diag.ptr.why: Direct sending reputation depends on matching reverse and forward DNS for the sending IP
mail.diag.ptr.fix: Ask the IP provider to align PTR and address records or use the relay setup
mail.diag.dnsbl.why: A documented DNSBL listing can affect direct delivery but does not establish current abuse
mail.diag.dnsbl.fix: Review the provider listing and removal policy or use the relay for sending
mail.diag.dnsbl_unknown.why: Unavailable or failed DNSBL controls cannot establish that an IP is unlisted
mail.diag.dnsbl_unknown.fix: Confirm provider access and resolver eligibility before enabling or repeating DNSBL queries
mail.diag.outbound.why: A failed TCP handshake cannot distinguish ISP filtering from routing or endpoint failure
mail.diag.outbound.fix: Review outbound TCP 25 with the network provider or use a relay when direct sending is unavailable
mail.diag.inbound.why: Direct receiving requires external reachability and a local probe cannot prove it
mail.diag.inbound.fix: Verify inbound TCP 25 from outside the LAN or review the receive-routing setup
mail.diag.client.why: Phone access depends on the actual app path, hostname, TLS and enabled mail services
mail.diag.client.fix: Check the app hostname, certificate and required services without assuming that its tunnel is unsupported
mail.diag.certificate.why: An expired mail-service certificate can prevent secure client connections
mail.diag.certificate.fix: Renew the certificate and assign it to the affected MailPlus service in DSM certificate settings

mail.setup.unreadable.notChecked: This version of the App does not check this, so it is not judged here. If it matters to you, check it in MailPlus Server yourself.
mail.setup.unreadable.noDomain: The check could not finish: DNS does not know this domain. Make sure the domain is spelled correctly and registered, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.notInMailPlus: The check could not finish: MailPlus Server has no such domain. Add the domain in MailPlus Server, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.dnsUnknown: The check could not finish: no DNS answer came back. Make sure the NAS can reach the internet, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.ipUnknown: The check could not finish: this NAS's public IP address could not be found. Make sure the NAS can reach the internet, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.ptrNone: The public IP has no reverse DNS name, so mail from it may be rejected. Ask your internet provider to set one that matches your mail host name, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.notStarted: MailPlus Server could not be read: it was busy, so the read did not start and nothing was sent. Wait a moment, then choose Check again.
mail.setup.unreadable: MailPlus Server could not be read
mail.setup.unreadable.timeout: MailPlus Server could not be read (timed out). DSM answered too slowly, which happens while the NAS is busy or short of memory. Check again when the NAS is less busy.
mail.setup.unreadable.authority: MailPlus Server could not be read: the read access given to this app is missing or no longer valid. Give read access again in Access settings, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.dsm: MailPlus Server could not be read: DSM refused the request. Make sure MailPlus Server is running and up to date, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.tooLarge: MailPlus Server could not be read: its reply was larger than this app accepts. Check again; if it repeats, the MailPlus setting with many entries (for example domains or relay hosts) is the cause.
mail.setup.unreadable.accountsTooLarge: MailPlus Server could not be read: this domain has more than 1000 accounts, more than this app reads, so whether an active account exists is unknown. Checking again gives the same result; set up this domain directly in MailPlus Server.
mail.setup.unreadable.unsupported: MailPlus Server could not be read: this MailPlus Server version does not offer the needed interface. Update MailPlus Server in Package Center, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.unavailable: MailPlus Server could not be read. Make sure MailPlus Server is running, then check again.
ui.wait.slow: Still reading. A busy NAS can take several minutes to answer; you can keep this window open.
ui.setup.previewProgress: Reading MailPlus Server and preparing the list of changes

mail.setup.unconfirmedBody: MailPlus Server did not answer in time, so it is not known whether the last change took effect. Nothing was sent again. Choose Roll back changes to try again: the assistant first reads the current settings and restores only what still matches this plan.
mail.setup.notStarted: MailPlus Server was too busy to start this step: this step sent nothing. Try again in a few minutes.
mail.setup.otherTransaction: Another administrator is applying or rolling back mail settings. Wait until that finishes, then try again.
mail.setup.rolledBackAfterTimeout: MailPlus Server did not answer in time while the changes were applied, so the assistant read the current settings and restored what this plan had changed.
mail.setup.rolledBackAfterProblem: A step could not be completed while the changes were applied, so the assistant restored what this plan had changed.
mail.setup.value.delivery.directFallback: Delivers directly; relay {hosts} only if that fails
mail.setup.value.fcrdns.fail: Name and address do not match
mail.setup.value.cloudflare.yes: Hosted on Cloudflare (source: DNS name servers)
mail.setup.value.cloudflare.no: Not hosted on Cloudflare (source: DNS name servers)
mail.setup.value.cloudflare.yesZone: Hosted on Cloudflare (source: your Cloudflare zone {zone} is active)
mail.setup.cause.noDomain: DNS does not know this domain
mail.setup.cause.notInMailPlus: MailPlus Server has no such domain
mail.setup.unknownFactsBody: These facts are needed to choose a mail path but are not known. The list says why for each; when they can be known, check again.
mail.diag.license_unchecked.why: This version of the assistant does not read which Synology Account the MailPlus licences are linked to, so that is not judged here
mail.setup.cause.ipUnknown: Public IP unknown, so not checked
mail.setup.cause.ptrNone: The public IP has no reverse DNS name
mail.setup.why.ipChanging: Because the public IP is known to change
mail.setup.why.ptrNone: Because the public IP has no reverse DNS name
mail.setup.why.fcrdnsFail: Because the reverse DNS does not match
mail.setup.why.dnsblListed: Because the public IP is on a blocklist
mail.setup.why.ipUnknown: Because the public IP could not be found
mail.setup.why.ptrUnknown: Because the reverse DNS could not be checked
mail.setup.why.fcrdnsUnknown: Because it could not be checked whether the reverse DNS matches
mail.setup.why.outboundUnknown: Because this NAS could not confirm that outgoing port 25 works
mail.setup.why.dnsblUnknown: Because the blocklists could not be checked
mail.setup.why.sendChecksPass: The reverse DNS matches, outgoing port 25 works and the IP is on no checked blocklist
mail.setup.planChanged: Your answers or the detected facts changed after this preview was prepared, so it was discarded. Generate the preview again
mail.setup.licenseShort: MailPlus Server has more active users than licences
mail.setup.licenseShortBody: MailPlus Server counts {active} active users but has {licensed} licences. Open MailPlus Server > License and add licences, or deactivate users under MailPlus Server > Account, then check again
mail.setup.value.license.short: {active} in use of {licensed}: more users than licences
mail.diag.license_unread.why: The licence counts could not be read from MailPlus Server, so licence use is not judged here
mail.setup.start: How will you set it up?
mail.setup.startBody: Choose what fits you; the wizard asks only what that way needs
mail.setup.start.own: I have my own domain and manage its DNS
mail.setup.start.ownHint: Type your domain, then choose how mail travels
mail.setup.start.cloudflare: Use Cloudflare (no domain yet, or the domain is already on Cloudflare)
mail.setup.start.cloudflareHint: Sign in once with a Cloudflare API token and pick your domain from a list
mail.setup.cloudflareBody: Create one API token in Cloudflare and paste it here once
mail.setup.cloudflare.tokenHint: Encrypted on the NAS at once and never shown again
mail.setup.cloudflare.connected: Signed in to Cloudflare. To use another token, paste it here
mail.setup.cloudflare.missing: This token lacks {permissions}. Cloudflare cannot add permissions to an existing token: press “{create}” to create a new one, then paste it on the sign-in step to replace this one
mail.setup.tokenInvalid: Cloudflare refused this token (unknown, expired or revoked). Check that it was copied in full, or create a new one
mail.setup.zoneBody: The domains in your Cloudflare account
mail.setup.zone.pendingNote: A domain still waiting can be chosen once its registrar uses the nameservers Cloudflare gave you; then check again
mail.setup.zone.noAccount: This token sees no Cloudflare account. Press “{create}” to create a new token in the account that holds your domain
mail.setup.zone.none: This Cloudflare account has no domain yet
mail.setup.zone.noneBody: Mail needs a domain. Register one on Cloudflare, then come back and check again
mail.setup.zone.noMatch: No zone of this Cloudflare account holds {domain}. Choose another account, or sign in with a token for the account that holds it
mail.setup.cloudflare.relayNote: The token is also the relay’s SMTP password: revoking it stops the relay and blocks a rollback
mail.setup.cloudflareUnavailable: Cloudflare did not give a clear answer just now, so nothing was concluded. Try again in a moment
mail.setup.tunnelChoice: Pick the tunnel that runs on this NAS or in its network. Only the delivery check after applying confirms it
mail.setup.tunnelHint: The tunnel must run on this NAS with host networking (as Syno Connect does): delivery is confirmed only from this NAS's own address. A wrong pick fails the delivery check, and you can roll back
mail.setup.tunnel.match: Connected from this NAS's public IP
mail.setup.lanUnknown: DSM does not name one connected private IPv4 address for this NAS, so inbound mail has no safe target. Check the network interface and default gateway in Control Panel › Network, then preview again
mail.setup.rulesLimit: Cloudflare allows 200 Email Routing rules per domain, and this zone's rules plus these addresses exceed that. Remove unused rules or enter fewer addresses
mail.setup.sendingPlan: This Cloudflare account's plan does not include sending mail: Cloudflare sends mail only on the Workers Paid plan (about USD 5 a month). Upgrade the account in Cloudflare and try again, or set up receiving only
mail.setup.sendingExisting: This mail domain is already in Cloudflare Email Sending, but it is turned off or its DNS records are not right. In Cloudflare, open Email Sending and fix it there (or delete it), then try again
mail.setup.routingConflict: The mail domain already receives mail elsewhere (an MX or SPF record), or an address already has an Email Routing rule. Nothing was changed. Remove the old setting first, or use other addresses
mail.setup.routingLeftover: An address already has an Email Routing rule left by an earlier setup of this assistant (named syno-home-keeper:…), and that setup's VPC Service sends to another address or over another Cloudflare Tunnel, so it may still carry another NAS's mail. It is not taken over, and nothing was changed. This needs manual cleanup: if that setup is no longer used, delete the rule and its Worker and VPC Service in the Cloudflare dashboard, then preview again
mail.setup.routingLeftoverDisabled: An address has a disabled Email Routing rule left by an earlier setup of this assistant (named syno-home-keeper:…). Taken over, it would stay disabled and the address would receive nothing; this assistant does not turn rules on. Nothing was changed. In the Cloudflare dashboard, enable or delete that rule, then preview again
mail.setup.inbound.direct: Delivered straight to MailPlus. While the NAS is offline, Cloudflare answers senders with a temporary error and they retry on their own schedule; nothing is stored in between
mail.setup.inbound.rollback: Rollback removes the Worker, the VPC Service and the address rules. Email Routing stays enabled on this domain with the MX and SPF records Cloudflare locked, and Cloudflare then refuses mail to these addresses
mail.setup.inbound.plan: Email Routing is free and Workers VPC is free during its beta. This path was tested on a Workers Paid account; on the Workers Free plan it is not verified
mail.setup.change.inbound.routing: Enable Email Routing for the mail domain
mail.setup.change.inbound.vpc: Register the NAS SMTP port 25 as a Workers VPC Service on the tunnel
mail.setup.change.inbound.rules: Route each address to the Worker
mail.setup.inbound.deliveredBody: A message to {address} came through Cloudflare and MailPlus recorded it as delivered
mail.setup.inbound.checkMail: Inbound mail is not confirmed yet
mail.setup.inbound.checkMailBody: From any outside mailbox, send a message to {address} with {code} in the subject, then choose Check again. Until it arrives in MailPlus, this setup is unverified
mail.setup.inbound.readbackFailed: The inbound setup could not be read back
mail.setup.inbound.readbackFailedBody: Email Routing, an address rule, the Worker, the VPC Service or a healthy tunnel is missing. Check again later, or roll back
mail.setup.inbound.logUnknown: MailPlus's transaction log could not be read
mail.setup.inbound.logUnknownBody: Delivery is unknown, not failed. Check again later
mail.setup.inbound.spf: SPF is checked against the NAS's own address, because the mail reaches MailPlus through the tunnel: a sender with an SPF record gets softfail (~all) or fail (-all). Unknown: whether that raises the spam score past the threshold, and whether MailPlus's SPF rejection refuses a fail, which the sender then gets back as a bounce. This setup changes no spam settings
mail.setup.cloudflare.readOnlyCheck: Sign-in checks read access only; if Cloudflare refuses a write later, setup names the permission and rolls back
mail.setup.inbound.relayNetworks: MailPlus Server has {count} networks that may send without signing in (often for printers or scanners). No change is needed: the Cloudflare receiving program hands MailPlus only mail addressed to this domain's mailboxes, so it cannot be used to forward mail elsewhere
mail.setup.inbound.relayNetworksUnknown: The networks MailPlus Server lets send without signing in could not be read. Nothing to do: the Cloudflare receiving program hands MailPlus only mail addressed to this domain's mailboxes
mail.setup.permissionRefused.zoneRead: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Zone → Zone → Read. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.dnsEdit: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Zone → DNS → Edit. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.sendingEdit: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Account → Email Sending → Edit. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.zoneSetting: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Zone → Zone Settings → Edit. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.routingRule: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Zone → Email Routing Rules → Edit. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.workersEdit: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Account → Workers Scripts → Edit. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.vpcAdmin: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Account → Connectivity Directory → Admin. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.permissionRefused.tunnelRead: Cloudflare refused this step because the token lacks Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Read. Create a new token with the link, sign in again with it, then run the setup again
mail.setup.zone.mailDomainHint: MailPlus Server's domains that are {zone} or under it
mail.setup.zone.mailDomainsUnknown: MailPlus Server's domains could not be read ({cause}), so the mail domain cannot be chosen yet. Check again
mail.setup.zone.reading: Reading the zone and MailPlus Server's domains
mail.setup.cause.notStarted: Not read (MailPlus Server was busy; nothing was sent)
mail.setup.cloudflare.oneRun: The token is encrypted and kept on this NAS. When you keep a setup that changed Cloudflare, it stays so “Sync mailboxes” and “Remove Cloudflare setup” work in one click; undoing or removing the setup deletes it
mail.setup.cloudflare.step1: Open the create-token form; the permissions are already filled in
mail.setup.cloudflare.step2: In Cloudflare, choose the account and the zone, then create the token and copy it
mail.setup.cloudflare.step2Hint: All zones by default; under Zone Resources you can keep only your mail domain’s zone
mail.setup.cloudflare.step3: Paste the token in the field below
mail.setup.route.headline: With or without a fixed IP, we can set up your mail
mail.setup.routeBody: Choose how mail reaches and leaves this NAS
mail.setup.route.cloudflare: Cloudflare receives and sends for me (recommended)
mail.setup.route.cloudflareHint: The NAS can be anywhere; no router setup
mail.setup.route.direct: Use my own IP to send and receive directly
mail.setup.route.directHint: Sends and receives directly; needs a fixed IP and port 25
mail.setup.route.fixedIpHint: Usually a separate request to your Internet provider; most home connections change their IP
mail.setup.route.inbound: Inbound TCP 25 reachable from outside, with the router forwarding it to this NAS
mail.setup.route.inboundHint: Many home providers block it. This wizard does not test from outside: check it with the link below
mail.setup.route.testNote: Opens MXToolbox’s SMTP test; the result is for you to judge, the wizard does not read it
mail.setup.route.notEligible: Not eligible? Cloudflare can receive and send for you without a fixed IP or port 25
mail.setup.route.checksDisagree: A detected result does not meet these requirements: even if you confirm, setup takes the Cloudflare path for that direction
mail.setup.why.routeCloudflare: Because you chose Cloudflare to receive and send
mail.setup.why.routeUnset: Because no route was chosen yet
mail.setup.why.routeDirect: You confirmed a fixed public IP and port 25 for your own IP
mail.setup.prereq.noDomainBody: Add {domain} in MailPlus Server and enable at least one account on it. The wizard checks again when you come back
mail.setup.prereq.noMailboxBody: Receiving and its check need at least one enabled mailbox on {domain}. Enable an account in MailPlus Server; the wizard checks again when you come back
mail.setup.prereq.receivePending: Receiving waits: {domain} has no enabled account
mail.setup.prereq.receivePendingBody: Sending needs no mailbox, so you can set it up now. Receiving needs at least one enabled mailbox on {domain}: enable one in MailPlus Server, then run setup again for receiving
mail.setup.facts.unrelated: Not needed for the chosen route ({count})
mail.setup.prereq.ready: MailPlus Server is ready for this domain
mail.setup.prereq.readyBody: Continue to choose how mail travels
ui.mailplus.title: MailPlus Server
ui.mailplus.overviewBody: This App needs MailPlus Server installed and running
ui.mailplus.wizardBody: Mail setup needs MailPlus Server installed and running before anything else.
ui.mailplus.ready: MailPlus Server is running. Continue with the setup.
ui.mailplus.launchRequested: DSM was asked to open Package Center. When you come back, this is checked again.
ui.mailplus.launchManual: This window cannot open Package Center: open Package Center from the DSM main menu.
ui.mailplus.notInstalled.title: MailPlus Server is not installed on this NAS
ui.mailplus.notInstalled.body: In Package Center, search for MailPlus Server and install it. Then come back here and check again.
ui.mailplus.stopped.title: MailPlus Server is stopped
ui.mailplus.stopped.body: In Package Center, open MailPlus Server and choose Run. Then come back here and check again.
ui.mailplus.broken.body: DSM reports the MailPlus Server installation as damaged. Repair MailPlus Server in Package Center, then come back here and check again.
ui.mailplus.unknown.title: Whether MailPlus Server runs could not be confirmed
ui.mailplus.unknown.body: DSM's package list could not be read: {cause}. Check again.
mail.mailplus.notInstalled: MailPlus Server is not installed on this NAS. Install it in Package Center, then check again.
mail.mailplus.stopped: MailPlus Server is stopped. Run it in Package Center, then check again.
mail.mailplus.unknown: MailPlus Server did not answer: it may have stopped or be updating. Check again.
mail.setup.cause.mailplusNotInstalled: Not read (MailPlus Server is not installed)
mail.setup.cause.mailplusApiMissing: Not read (MailPlus Server did not answer; it may have stopped or be updating)
mail.setup.unreadable.mailplusNotInstall: MailPlus Server is not installed on this NAS. Install it in Package Center, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.mailplusStopped: MailPlus Server is stopped. Run it in Package Center, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.mailplusApiMissing: MailPlus Server did not answer: it may have stopped or be updating. Make sure it is running in Package Center, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.dsmPermission: MailPlus Server could not be read: DSM denied permission. Sign in to DSM as an administrator, then check again.
mail.setup.unreadable.dsmSession: MailPlus Server could not be read: the DSM sign-in expired. Sign in to DSM again, then choose Check again.
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_missing.title: MailPlus Server is not installed
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_missing.body: Without it, no mail can be sent or received
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_missing.actio: Install MailPlus Server in Package Center
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_stopped.title: MailPlus Server is stopped
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_stopped.body: While it is stopped, no mail is sent or received
mail.diag.problem.mailplus_stopped.actio: Start MailPlus Server in Package Center
mail.diag.problem.smtp_off.title: SMTP is turned off in MailPlus Server
mail.diag.problem.smtp_off.body: Mail to and from other servers cannot get through
mail.diag.problem.smtp_off.action: Turn on SMTP in the MailPlus Server settings
mail.diag.problem.relay_stopped.title: The sending relay has stopped
mail.diag.problem.relay_stopped.body: Mail sent through it waits in the queue
mail.diag.problem.relay_stopped.action: Set up sending again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.queue_stuck.title: Mail has waited over an hour to be sent
mail.diag.problem.queue_stuck.body: The recipients have not received these messages yet
mail.diag.problem.queue_stuck.action: Open the queue in MailPlus Server to see why they were not sent
mail.diag.problem.deliver_auth.title: The relay server refused the sign-in
mail.diag.problem.deliver_auth.body: Mail to outside addresses cannot be sent
mail.diag.problem.deliver_auth.action: Check the user name and password the relay uses
mail.diag.problem.deliver_dns.title: The NAS cannot look up the receiving server
mail.diag.problem.deliver_dns.body: Mail to outside addresses is delayed or fails
mail.diag.problem.deliver_dns.action: Check the DNS server in Control Panel > Network
mail.diag.problem.deliver_tls.title: The secure connection failed while sending
mail.diag.problem.deliver_tls.body: Mail to outside addresses cannot be sent
mail.diag.problem.deliver_tls.action: Check the relay server's port and encryption
mail.diag.problem.deliver_policy.title: Receiving servers refused your mail
mail.diag.problem.deliver_policy.body: They may treat it as spam
mail.diag.problem.deliver_policy.action: See the refusal reason in the MailPlus Server queue
mail.diag.problem.deliver_remote.title: Receiving servers are not accepting mail right now
mail.diag.problem.deliver_remote.body: Sending is retried automatically, so mail may arrive late
mail.diag.problem.deliver_remote.action: Wait for the retries; if it still fails after a day, check the MailPlus Server queue
mail.diag.problem.spf.title: The SPF record is missing or wrong
mail.diag.problem.spf.body: Receiving servers may bounce your mail or mark it as spam
mail.diag.problem.spf.action: Set up sending again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.dkim.title: The DKIM signing record is missing or invalid
mail.diag.problem.dkim.body: Receiving servers cannot confirm that the mail really comes from you
mail.diag.problem.dkim.action: Set up sending again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.dmarc.title: The DMARC record is not valid
mail.diag.problem.dmarc.body: Receiving servers may bounce your mail or mark it as spam
mail.diag.problem.dmarc.action: Set up sending again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.mx.title: The domain says it accepts no mail
mail.diag.problem.mx.body: Mail sent to you from outside does not arrive
mail.diag.problem.mx.action: Set up receiving again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.inbound.title: Outside servers cannot reach port 25 on the NAS
mail.diag.problem.inbound.body: Mail sent to you from outside does not arrive
mail.diag.problem.inbound.action: Set up receiving again in the mail setup wizard
mail.diag.problem.ptr.title: The NAS's public IP address has no matching reverse DNS
mail.diag.problem.ptr.body: Receiving servers may refuse mail the NAS sends directly
mail.diag.problem.ptr.action: Send through a relay with the mail setup wizard, or ask your internet provider to set the reverse DNS
mail.diag.problem.dnsbl.title: The NAS's public IP address is on a spam block list
mail.diag.problem.dnsbl.body: Receiving servers may refuse mail the NAS sends directly
mail.diag.problem.dnsbl.action: Send through a relay with the mail setup wizard, or ask the list to remove the address
mail.diag.problem.imap_off.title: IMAP is turned off in MailPlus Server
mail.diag.problem.imap_off.body: Phone apps and mail programs cannot get mail
mail.diag.problem.imap_off.action: Turn on IMAP in the MailPlus Server settings
mail.diag.problem.phone.title: Phone apps cannot reach the mail server
mail.diag.problem.phone.body: Mail cannot be read or sent from the phone
mail.diag.problem.phone.action: Check the server address and port in the app, and that the service is on in MailPlus Server
mail.diag.problem.cert_expired.title: The mail server's certificate has expired
mail.diag.problem.cert_expired.body: Phone apps and mail programs may refuse to connect
mail.diag.problem.cert_expired.action: Renew the certificate in Control Panel > Security > Certificate
mail.diag.problem.cert_soon.title: The mail server's certificate expires within 30 days
mail.diag.problem.cert_soon.body: After that, phone apps and mail programs may refuse to connect
mail.diag.problem.cert_soon.action: Renew the certificate in Control Panel > Security > Certificate
mail.diag.problem.account_inactive.title: The mailbox account is not activated
mail.diag.problem.account_inactive.body: This account cannot send or receive mail
mail.diag.problem.account_inactive.actio: Activate the account on the account page of MailPlus Server
mail.diag.problem.home_access.title: The mailbox's home folder cannot be opened
mail.diag.problem.home_access.body: This account cannot send or receive mail
mail.diag.problem.home_access.action: Turn on the user home service in Control Panel > User & Group > Advanced
mail.diag.problem.source_blocked.title: DSM auto block has blocked the mail program's IP address
mail.diag.problem.source_blocked.body: That device cannot sign in, even with the right password
mail.diag.problem.source_blocked.action: Remove the address in Control Panel > Security > Protection > Auto Block
mail.diag.problem.license_count.title: More users are activated than there are licenses
mail.diag.problem.license_count.body: Users over the limit may not be able to use mail
mail.diag.problem.license_count.action: Add licenses in MailPlus Server > License, or deactivate users who do not need mail
mail.diag.problem.license_owner.title: The MailPlus licenses belong to another Synology Account
mail.diag.problem.license_owner.body: The licenses may not count for this NAS
mail.diag.problem.license_owner.action: Check the linked Synology Account in MailPlus Server > License
mail.diag.other.queue: {count} messages wait in the queue and are retried automatically
mail.diag.other.dmarc_missing: No DMARC record (recommended, helps keep mail out of spam): {targets}
mail.diag.other.mx_missing: No MX record (needed only to receive mail directly): {targets}
mail.diag.other.outbound: Could not confirm that the NAS can send mail directly (port 25)
ui.diag.verdict.unclear: No clear problem found; some items cannot be checked automatically
ui.diag.next.title: What to try next
ui.diag.next.cannot-send: Send a test message to an outside address; if it does not arrive, look at the queue in MailPlus Server
ui.diag.next.bounce-or-spam: Open the bounce message and read the reason the receiving server gives
ui.diag.next.cannot-receive: Send yourself a message from an outside address, then check the mail log in MailPlus Server
ui.diag.next.phone-connect: In the phone app, check the server address, port, user name and password
ui.diag.next.not-sure: Choose a more specific problem and check again for a sharper result
ui.diag.launchManual: This window cannot open it: open it from the DSM main menu
ui.diag.limits: These checks only read settings, so they cannot find every cause
mail.setup.receive.title: How mail is received
mail.setup.receive.domainBody: Mail to any address @{domain} goes to MailPlus Server. Adding or removing users needs nothing more
mail.setup.receive.addressesBody: Only the {count} current MailPlus mailboxes receive. After adding or removing users, press Sync mailboxes on the Overview
mail.setup.receive.subdomain: Needs the main domain (for example example.com); a subdomain cannot be received as a whole
mail.setup.receive.inUse: This domain already sends its other addresses somewhere on Cloudflare; that setting is left as it is
mail.setup.receive.unknown: Could not be checked right now; use chosen mailboxes, or go back and try again
mail.setup.receive.domainUnavailable: The whole domain cannot be received: it is not the main domain, or its other addresses already go somewhere else. Go back and choose Chosen mailboxes
mail.setup.consequence.receiveDomain: Receiving: mail to any address @{domain} goes to MailPlus Server
mail.setup.change.inbound.catchall: Send mail to any address @{domain} to the inbound Worker
mail.inbound.tokenRequired: A Cloudflare token is needed to sync. Paste one below
mail.inbound.cause.mailplus: MailPlus Server's users could not be read, so nothing was changed
mail.inbound.cause.token: Cloudflare did not accept the saved token
mail.inbound.cause.gone: This domain's receiving setup is no longer on Cloudflare; run the setup again
mail.inbound.cause.interrupted: The sync was interrupted before it finished
mail.inbound.cause.cloudflare: Cloudflare did not answer in time
ui.inbound.title: On Cloudflare
ui.inbound.body: Domains that send or receive mail through Cloudflare. Uninstalling keeps these settings; to undo them, press Remove
ui.inbound.hint: MailPlus user changes sync by themselves within about 10 minutes; press to sync now
ui.inbound.inLine: All mailboxes are already in sync; nothing changed
ui.inbound.tokenBody: The saved token is missing or was refused. Create one with the same button as in the setup, then paste it here
ui.inbound.tokenHint: Checked with Cloudflare, then sealed on this NAS; it is never shown again
ui.remove.title: Remove the Cloudflare setup of {domain}?
ui.remove.body: Only what this App created is removed or put back:
ui.remove.kept: Anything else on Cloudflare stays as it is. Mail to this domain may stop arriving until it is set up again.
ui.remove.routing: Also turn off Cloudflare receiving for this domain
ui.remove.routingBody: This App turned it on during setup. Cloudflare then stops accepting any mail for the domain and deletes the MX and SPF records it added for receiving.
ui.remove.done: The Cloudflare setup of {domain} was removed and MailPlus Server put back as it was before the setup
ui.remove.failed: Removal stopped: {cause}. What is already done is not repeated; try again.
ui.remove.access: Removal stopped: putting MailPlus Server back needs {profile}, which this App is not allowed yet. Allow access, then try again. What is already done is not repeated.
ui.remove.uninstall: Uninstalling the App keeps these settings on Cloudflare; removing them here is the way to undo them
ui.remove.item.receiveDomain: Receiving for the whole domain: the mail program and connection on Cloudflare; the domain’s earlier receiving setting is put back
ui.remove.item.receiveAddresses: Receiving for the listed mailboxes: the mail program, the connection and this App’s mailbox entries on Cloudflare
ui.remove.item.sending: Sending through Cloudflare for this domain
ui.remove.item.dns: The DNS records this App added
ui.remove.item.mailplus: MailPlus Server settings this App changed, put back as they were before the setup
ui.remove.item.relay: The mail forwarding service of this App is turned off
ui.remove.item.token: The saved Cloudflare token is deleted from this NAS
mail.remove.cause.changed: something this App created was changed on Cloudflare since, so it is left as it is
mail.remove.cause.nas: a setting on this NAS (MailPlus Server or the forwarding service) could not be put back
mail.remove.cause.authority: this App has not been allowed to change MailPlus Server's settings
mail.remove.cause.admin: only an administrator can put MailPlus Server's settings back
mail.remove.cause.mailplus: MailPlus Server's settings could not be put back
mail.remove.cause.relay: the forwarding service on this NAS could not be stopped
mail.remove.cause.record: this App’s record of the setup could not be read or saved
mail.diag.token_invalid.title: Cloudflare refused the saved token
mail.diag.token.why: The relay logs in to Cloudflare with this token, and the mailbox sync and the removal use it too
mail.diag.token.fix: Enter a new Cloudflare token on the Overview
mail.diag.problem.token_invalid.title: The Cloudflare token no longer works
mail.diag.problem.token_invalid.body: It may have been deleted in Cloudflare. Sending through Cloudflare and the mailbox sync are paused; mail waits in the MailPlus queue
mail.diag.problem.token_invalid.action: Create a new token and enter it once; it replaces the old one everywhere
ui.token.invalid: Cloudflare token no longer works (it may have been deleted); sending and sync are paused
ui.token.invalidNoRelay: Cloudflare token no longer works (it may have been deleted); sync and removal are paused
ui.token.queued: Mail MailPlus could not send stays in its queue for up to 48 hours; save a new token before then and it is sent at the next retry
ui.token.title: New Cloudflare token for {domain}
ui.token.body: The new token replaces the old one everywhere this setup uses it: sending through Cloudflare, Sync mailboxes and Remove Cloudflare setup
ui.token.missing: This token lacks: {permissions}. Create one with the button above, which fills them in
mail.inbound.tokenMissing: The token lacks a permission this setup needs. Create one with the setup's button, which fills them all in
ui.setup.tokenBody: It may have been deleted, or it lacks a permission, so the changes on Cloudflare cannot be undone. Enter a new token, then roll back again
ui.setup.tokenSaved: New token saved. Choose Roll back again
mail.setup.unsafe.zoneMismatch: The Cloudflare token does not open the account that holds this domain. Check the domain and use a token from that account
mail.setup.unsafe.inboundExists: Cloudflare already has a receiving program or connection with this App’s name that this setup did not create. Remove it on Cloudflare, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.sendingDns: Cloudflare reports a problem with this domain’s Email Sending records. Fix the domain under Email Sending on Cloudflare, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.egressUnknown: This NAS’s public IP address could not be found, so the SPF record cannot be written. Check the NAS’s internet connection, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.dkimUnknown: MailPlus Server’s DKIM key for this domain could not be read. Turn on DKIM for the domain in MailPlus Server, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.dnsExists: A DNS record this setup needs to add already exists on Cloudflare with other content. It is left as it is; check it on Cloudflare, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.relayInUse: Mail forwarding through Cloudflare is already set up and working on this NAS. It is left as it is so mail keeps flowing
mail.setup.unsafe.mailplusReply: MailPlus Server replied in a way this App does not understand, so nothing was changed. Update MailPlus Server, then try again
mail.setup.unsafe.savedRecord: This App’s saved record of the setup does not match what it finds now, so it changes nothing. Run the diagnosis to see what differs
mail.setup.unsafe.planCheck: The planned change no longer matches the current settings, so it was not applied. Start the setup again to make a fresh plan
mail.setup.unsafe.secret: A key this setup saved could not be read back, so it stopped. Start the setup again
ui.remove.item.receiveDNS: The receiving MX and SPF records Cloudflare added for this subdomain at setup (a record that was there before is kept or put back)
ui.remove.locked.title: Some receiving records were left on Cloudflare
ui.remove.locked.body: Cloudflare locks these MX records of {domain} for Email Routing and does not allow deleting them, so they were left in place:
ui.remove.locked.where: To remove them, open Email Routing on Cloudflare, select {zone}, then open Settings
ui.remove.locked.whereAny: To remove them, open Email Routing on Cloudflare, select the domain, then open Settings
ui.remove.locked.warning: Turning off Email Routing there may stop receiving for the whole domain, not only this subdomain
ui.setup.authority.failed: “{step}” could not be done because this App lacks {access}. Allow access, then try again
ui.setup.authority.rolledBack: “{step}” could not be done because this App lacks {access}. The changes made before it were put back. Allow access, then run the setup again
mail.setup.planned.routing: Cloudflare Email Routing adds this name's MX and SPF records
mail.setup.planned.sending: Cloudflare Email Sending adds its sending records under this name
mail.setup.planned.dns: The setup adds this DNS record in Cloudflare
mail.setup.planned.mailplusDomain: The setup creates this mail domain in MailPlus Server
mail.setup.optional.dmarc: Not needed to send. Without its own DMARC record, the parent domain's policy applies
mail.setup.optional.spfRelay: Not needed to send through Cloudflare: Email Sending is checked against its own records
mail.setup.zone.help.firstRun.title: Finish MailPlus Server's first setup with {zone}
mail.setup.zone.help.firstRun.body: MailPlus Server has not been set up yet. Open it and, where its setup wizard asks for the basic SMTP settings, enter these values
mail.setup.zone.help.addDomain.title: Add {zone} to MailPlus Server
mail.setup.zone.help.addDomain.body: MailPlus Server has no mail domain in {zone}. Open it, go to Domain, create this domain (or a name under it), and enable the accounts that should use it
mail.setup.zone.help.either.title: MailPlus Server has no mail domain in {zone}
mail.setup.zone.help.either.body: Open MailPlus Server. If its setup wizard asks for the basic SMTP settings, enter these values; otherwise go to Domain and create this domain
mail.setup.zone.help.after: When you come back to this window, the App checks again by itself
ui.mailplus.notSetUp: Choose the domain in this App first, then follow its steps to finish MailPlus setup
mail.inbound.auto.cause.mailplus: MailPlus Server's mailbox list could not be read
mail.inbound.auto.cause.stopped: MailPlus Server is not running (it may be updating or restarting)
mail.inbound.auto.cause.changed: MailPlus Server answered in a format this App does not expect (it may have been updated)
mail.inbound.auto.cause.empty: MailPlus Server reports no mailboxes in this domain
mail.inbound.auto.cause.approval: This App's system access needs to be approved again
ui.inbound.autoStopped: Automatic sync is paused: {cause}. Once MailPlus Server works normally, press Sync mailboxes
ui.inbound.held: {count} mailboxes are no longer in MailPlus Server; automatic sync left their routing rules. Sync mailboxes will delete these {count} rules
ui.inbound.heldEmpty: {cause}, so automatic sync deleted no rule. If that is right, Sync mailboxes will delete all {count} rules
mail.setup.change.mailplus.domain: Create the mail domain {domain} in MailPlus Server (no users yet; Remove deletes it while it has none)
ui.remove.item.mailplusDomain: The MailPlus Server mail domain this App created (kept if it has users)
ui.remove.keptDomain: The MailPlus Server mail domain {domain} has users now, so it was kept. Delete it in MailPlus Server if you no longer need it.
mail.setup.zone.newDomain: Create a MailPlus Server mail domain…
mail.setup.zone.newDomainInvalid: Enter a domain name, such as {zone}
mail.setup.zone.newDomainOutside: The mail domain must be {zone} or a name under it
mail.setup.zone.newDomainExists: MailPlus Server already has this mail domain: choose it above
mail.setup.zone.newDomainNote: The preview adds a step that creates {domain} in MailPlus Server; nothing is created until you confirm. The new domain has no users yet: to receive mail, add users to it in MailPlus Server.
mail.setup.prereq.receivePendingNew: Receiving waits: {domain} is a new mail domain with no users yet
mail.setup.prereq.receivePendingNewBody: Sending needs no mailbox, so you can finish sending now; the setup creates {domain} in MailPlus Server. To receive, add users to {domain} in MailPlus Server, then run the setup again.
ui.cfFlow.title: How Cloudflare mail works
ui.cfFlow.workerTip: Email Routing can only forward to verified addresses or a Worker, not directly to a private network over SMTP
ui.cfFlow.stageLabel: Cloudflare mail send and receive flow diagram
